- Create a complete, playable 3D lightsaber-building game where players choose each component and kyber crystal, then sell the saber to see its value.

- Build it now without clarification; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save any verification screenshots as small JPEGs no wider than 1280px.

- Implemented 3D saber assembly, five component-selection steps, value calculation, sound toggle, and sell flow in `game.js`.
- Started a local server and opened the app in Playwright; generated `screenshots/forge.jpg`.
- Adjusted the 3D camera framing and added a data-URI favicon after the first browser check.

- Verify the updated camera framing and exercise the build/sell interactions in the browser.

- (none)

1. Capture and inspect an updated `screenshots/forge.jpg`.

3. Report the game features, assumptions, and verification results.

- `index.html`: Game page structure and UI.
- `styles.css`: Responsive visual design and layout.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene and game logic.

- The game runs locally at `http://localhost:3002`; changes are uncommitted.
- `node --check game.js` passed. The first browser load showed only a missing favicon 404, subsequently addressed.

## Objective
- Complete and verify the customizable 3D lightsaber-building game and its simulated auction.

## Requirements
- Add substantially more customization options and improve visuals.
- Use six named bidders, visible offers, and an accept-offer control.
- Save verification screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Keep the game as a standalone browser experience using Three.js and fictional Galactic Credits.
- Use a timed in-browser auction.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added nine builder categories, including metal accents, blade profile, activation switch, and engraving, with associated 3D model changes.
- Added the auction room, six bidders, simulated bidding, offer acceptance, auction breakdown, and reset flow.
- Fixed dynamic builder step counts and added the missing `id="auctionRoom"` plus nine-step HTML defaults.
- Browser check confirmed nine steps, rendered canvas, hidden loading state, and no console errors.
- Verified simulated bids appeared and accepting an offer showed the sold result; reset returned the builder to its initial selection and step.

### Active
- Finish responsive auction-room verification and capture updated JPEG verification screenshot(s) no wider than 1280px.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Reopen the auction and verify its layout and controls at mobile width; check reset behavior without racing the overlay transition.
2. Capture and inspect updated builder and auction JPEG screenshots, each no wider than 1280px.
3. Run final syntax/status checks and report assumptions briefly.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Builder and auction markup; dynamic step defaults and auction room ID.
- `game.js`: Builder options, 3D assembly, pricing, and auction logic.
- `auction.css`: Auction visuals and responsive styles.
- `styles.css`: Builder layout and shared overlay styling.
- `screenshots/`: Existing screenshots are older than the recent changes.

- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Complete and verify the customizable 3D lightsaber-building game and its simulated auction.

## Requirements
- Add substantially more customization options and improve visuals.
- Use six named bidders, visible offers, and an accept-offer control.
- Save verification screenshots as JPEGs no wider than 1280px.
- Make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them when finished.

## Decisions
- Keep the game as a standalone browser experience using Three.js and fictional Galactic Credits.
- Use a timed in-browser auction.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added nine builder categories, including metal accents, blade profile, activation switch, and engraving, with associated 3D model changes.
- Added the auction room, six bidders, simulated bidding, offer acceptance, auction breakdown, and reset flow.
- Fixed dynamic builder step counts and added `id="auctionRoom"` plus nine-step HTML defaults.
- Browser checks confirmed nine steps, rendered canvas, hidden loading state, and no console errors; simulated bids and sold-result flow were verified.
- Adjusted mobile auction room height to fit the viewport and added `body.sale-active` overflow locking plus removal on close.

### Active
- Verify the updated mobile auction layout and whether the `body.sale-active` scroll lock takes effect.
- Capture and inspect fresh builder and auction JPEG screenshots, each no wider than 1280px.
- Verify reset behavior after the sold-result transition; final syntax/status checks remain.

- (none)

1. Retest the mobile auction after the latest CSS/JS edits; computed body overflow was still `auto` despite the `sale-active` class.

3. Test reset after the result overlay transition, then run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`.

- `index.html`: Builder and auction markup.
- `game.js`: Builder options, 3D assembly, pricing, and auction/reset logic.
- `auction.css`: Auction visuals and responsive styles.
- `styles.css`: Builder layout and shared overlay styling.
- `screenshots/auction-mobile.jpg`: Existing mobile JPEG, captured before the latest responsive/scroll-lock edits.
- `screenshots/forge.jpg`: Older builder screenshot.

- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed the project files as untracked.
